title: Maryland PSC Order No. 92503 (Case No. 9888)
text:
ORDER NO. 92503 

Baltimore Gas and Electric Company’s 
Application for Adjustments to Its Electric 
Base Rates 

_________________________________ 
* 
* 
* 
* 
* 
* 
* 

BEFORE THE 
PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION 
OF MARYLAND 
_____________ 

CASE NO. 9888 
_____________ 
Issue Date: July 6, 2026 

ORDER INITIATING DOCKET, SUSPENDING TARIFF REVISIONS, AND 
SCHEDULING PREHEARING CONFERENCE 

On July 2, 2026,1 Baltimore Gas and Electric Company (“BGE”) submitted to the 
Commission an application for authority to adjust its electric base rates and other revisions 
to its Electric Service Tariffs designated “Supplement 754 to P.S.C. Md. E-6 (Electric)” in 
its Maryland service territory pursuant to Annotated Code of Maryland, Public Utilities 
Article (“PUA”) §§ 4-203 and 4-204 (“Application”). In support of its Application, BGE 
also filed supporting testimony, exhibits, and data required by the Commission’s general 
filing requirements, and proposed rate schedules to be effective August 1, 2026. 
BGE provides evidentiary support for an electric revenue deficiency of $156.1 
million.2 The revenue deficiency demonstrated is based on a test year for the 12 months 
ended March 31, 2026, would lead to an overall return on equity of 7.68 percent. 

1 Maillog No. 331766. 
2 BGE states that “[i]n testimony and exhibits supporting this Application, BGE provides evidentiary support 
for an electric revenue deficiency of $156.1 million. The revenue deficiency demonstrated is based on a test 
year for the 12 months ended March 31, 2026 (adjusted for certain known and measurable changes), a return 
on equity of 10.4 percent, and an overall rate of return on investment of 7.68 percent. If granted in full, the 
requested rate adjustment would result in an overall increase of 2.8 percent in total electric bills, but the 
impact will vary from rate schedule to rate schedule and from customer to customer. The total monthly bill 
for a residential electric customer with average monthly usage of 851 kWh is expected to increase by about 
four percent (or about $8.00) per month.” Id. at 4-5. 

2 
A prehearing conference in this matter is hereby set for Tuesday, August 11, 2026, 
at 11:00 a.m., in the Frank O. Heintz Hearing Room, 16th Floor, William Donald Schaefer 
Tower, 6 St. Paul Street, Baltimore, Maryland. The purpose of the hearing is to set a 
procedural schedule for this proceeding, consider any petitions to intervene that have been 
filed, and consider any other preliminary matters requested by the parties. Petitions to 
intervene shall be filed by Monday, August 7, 2026. Furthermore, discovery commences 
immediately for BGE, the Commission’s Technical Staff (“Staff”), and the Maryland 
Office of People’s Counsel (“OPC”). 
IT IS, THEREFORE, this 6th day of July in the year Two Thousand Twenty-Six, 
by the Public Service Commission of Maryland, ORDERED: 
(1) 
that proceedings to consider the Application and the justness and 
reasonableness of Baltimore Gas and Electric Company’s Application are hereby instituted 
by the Commission; 
(2) 
that, pursuant to PUA § 4-204(b)(2), the tariff revisions filed by BGE are 
suspended for an initial period of 180 days from August 1, 2026; 
(3) 
that discovery commences immediately for BGE, the Commission’s 
Technical Staff and the Maryland Office of People’s Counsel; 
(4) 
that 
interested 
parties 
shall 
file 
petitions 
to 
intervene 
by 
August 7, 2026; 
(5) 
that BGE is hereby directed to cause a display advertisement to be published 
in a newspaper(s) in general circulation throughout its service area at least two times prior 
to August 1, 2026, that includes a description of the matter on which the prehearing 
conference is being held and the time, date, method, and purpose of the prehearing 

3 
conference scheduled for August 11, 2026. The notice shall also advise persons who seek 
to intervene in this proceeding that any petition to intervene shall be filed3 by August 7, 
2026, with Andrew S. Johnston, Executive Secretary, Maryland Public Service 
Commission, William Donald Schaefer Tower, 6 St. Paul Street, 16th Floor, Baltimore, 
Maryland 21202 and reference “Case No. 9888” in the subject line; 
(6) 
that BGE shall file a proof of publication on or before the date of the 
prehearing conference; 
(7) 
that BGE also shall place on its home page a notice of the prehearing 
conference and the date by which petitions to intervene in the matter must be filed in a 
manner that a customer need not click the link to determine the date, time, method, and 
purpose of the prehearing conference or the date by which a petition to intervene must be 
filed; and 
(8) 
that BGE is directed to employ any routinely used social media platforms, 
such as Twitter or Facebook, and any other means of communication at its disposal to 
further notify its customers of the prehearing conference, as appropriate. 

By Direction of the Commission, 
/s/ Andrew S. Johnston 
Andrew S. Johnston 
Executive Secretary 

3 Details of the E-file system are on the Commission’s web page, www.psc.maryland.gov.
